chunks.text:
Reductionism concerns relations between entities, explanations, or theories at different levels. A connection with compression: explaining several patterns through common underlying processes. The link to becoming remains an open question.

Ontology: higher-level entities consist of lower-level entities. A biological example is the claim that organisms consist entirely of physical components and their interactions. This makes no claim about a minimum number of parts.
Methodology: investigate a system by studying its components and their interactions. Whether this strategy answers a particular question has to be established in that context.
Theory: recover one theory’s claims from another. In Nagel’s account, this involves derivation, sometimes using bridge principles connecting their terms. Corrections and approximations can be part of the relation; the theories’ ages do not define it.

These claims can come apart: accepting physical composition alone does not establish that every biological explanation can be reduced to physics. See reductionism in biology, §1⁠ and scientific reduction, §2⁠.
